Maya (Sapphire): Hey team — hitting intermittent p99 spikes on our inference calls since ~09:10 UTC, affecting production. Requests that usually finish ~200ms are spiking to 2-5s. Can you triage? :frowning:
Alice C (Customer Success): Thanks for the heads up, Maya. Raising this with infra/SRE now. Can you paste a couple of example request_ids from your logs?
Maya (Sapphire): Sure — one example: req=sh-req-20260315-9f3a2, another: sh-req-20260315-9f4b9. Payloads are standard chat completions, ~600 tokens context. No recent config changes on our side.
IncidentBot: Alert created: tail-latency-high channel=customer-success sev=low marker=auto-20260315-0912
Rob S (SRE): looking. Can someone share the exact API endpoint+model? Also are they on Dedicated or Hosted?
Maya (Sapphire): Hosted API - model gpt-rl-13b, region=us-west-2, tenant_id=sapphire-prod
Priya R (Runtime): I see an unusual pattern in router logs around those timestamps — bursts of large batches for tenant=sapphire and a handful of long-running worker calls. Posting a snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:31.124Z [router] request_id=sh-req-20260315-9f3a2 tenant=sapphire model=gpt-rl-13b latency_ms=2431 route=default
2026-03-15T09:12:31.128Z [worker-gpu-7] request_id=sh-req-20260315-9f3a2 gpu=7 batch_size=56 kv_cache_miss=1 decode_ms=1987
2026-03-15T09:12:31.130Z [router] request_id=sh-req-20260315-9f4b9 tenant=sapphire model=gpt-rl-13b latency_ms=3145 route=default
```
Priya R (Runtime): batch_size=56 for 13B is high for our soft-latency SLO. Looks like a large embedding/rerank job or a mis-tagged bulk request hitting the same queue.
Rob S (SRE): @Jordan any recent config that could let tenant-level traffic accumulate on a single worker? Thinking sticky routing or missing per-tenant concurrency caps.
Jordan L (Platform): We had a routing tweak last week to reduce cross-tenant tail by preferring warm workers, but that shouldn't increase single-tenant burstiness. However I do see a missed per-tenant throttle entry for tenant=sapphire between 09:09–09:14 due to a rules-engine NPE we patched earlier today — that allowed higher concurrency than policy. Pasting rule excerpt:
```
# intended
tenant_limits:
  sapphire:
    max_concurrency: 12
    priority: normal
# observed (due to rules-engine bug)
tenant_limits:
  sapphire: null
```
Rob S (SRE): that explains it. Without the cap, their client was able to pile up requests that got combined into big batches, hurting tail latency. Potential noisy-neighbor symptom.
Maya (Sapphire): oh wow — we did kick off a background rerank sweep early this morning (internal), but it should have been rate-limited. Looks like our client retry/backoff may be too aggressive. We'll throttle on our side too.
Alice C (Customer Success): Action plan proposal: short-term mitigate in-hosted platform, and long-term add guardrails + alerting. Thoughts?
Priya R (Runtime): Short-term mitigations I can do in <30m:
- Enforce per-tenant concurrency cap immediately (hotfix to rules service)
- Add a temporary per-tenant max_batch_size override: sapphire -> 16
- Route sapphire traffic to a larger pool (scale up) or fallback to gpt-rl-7b-quant for non-critical routes
I can push a config change and roll it to us-west-2.
Rob S (SRE): I'll hold for the change window. Also suggest enabling a quick circuit breaker that rejects requests over a soft qps for 5 minutes to let the system recover.
Jordan L (Platform): Deploying a conservative patch now. Patch diff:
```
--- a/routing/rules.yaml
+++ b/routing/rules.yaml
@@
- tenant_limits:
-  sapphire: null
+ tenant_limits:
+  sapphire:
+    max_concurrency: 12
+    max_batch_size: 16
+    fallback_model: gpt-rl-7b-quant
```
Jordan L (Platform): Rolling to us-west-2 -> canary 10% -> 30% -> 100%. ETA ~14m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
IncidentBot: Deploy started by Jordan L (Platform) to us-west-2 canary=10% change_id=chg-20260315-8873
Rob S (SRE): While rolling, I'm going to add an autoscaling bump for the router frontends handling Sapphire so batches don't form while rules propagate.
Priya R (Runtime): Also adding a temporary route-level pack size limiter so even if concurrency is high, batch_size will be cut.
Kevin (Sapphire-Eng): We're seeing immediate improvement after your initial change, thanks. p99 dropped from ~3.1s to ~420ms in our dashboards. We'll also patch our internal sweep to obey per-tenant QPS.
Maya (Sapphire): Confirming improvements on our side too. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:
Alice C (Customer Success): Long-term items to track:
- Add automated detection for when a single tenant's batch_size jumps above threshold
- Customer-side best-practices doc for bulk jobs (recommended backoff, dedicated endpoints)
- Consider per-tenant priority tiers and opt-in dedicated pools for heavy batch customers
Rob S (SRE): I'll file a post-incident ticket with repro steps and metrics. Attaching repro commands for QA/Sapphire to validate fixes:
```
# synthetic load that reproduced the issue
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SAHPR_KEY" \
    -H "X-Tenant-ID: sapphire" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-rl-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test payload"}],"max_tokens":200}' &
done
wait
```
Rob S (SRE): QA note: run with concurrent=200-ish from a small fleet to see batching behavior. Expect high batch sizes if throttles missing.
Priya R (Runtime): Observability work: add per-tenant time-series for batch_size, kv_cache_hits, and worker_decode_ms. Also add an alert: tenant_batch_size > 32 for 2+ minutes -> paged to eng-sre.
Jordan L (Platform): We'll also add a canary for rules engine to detect null rules entries on deploy. That NPE was the root cause of the missing throttle.
Alice C (Customer Success): Assigned followups:
- Rob: incident writeup + RCA (due EOD)
- Priya: observability alerts + temporary config TTL (done)
- Jordan: rules-engine canary + postmortem (in progress)
- Maya/Kevin: customer-side mitigation and confirmation (in progress)
Maya (Sapphire): We'll also share our internal scheduler config so Redwood can suggest best-practice knobs.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved: tail-latency-high change_id=chg-20260315-8873 status=resolved duration=00:20:25
Rob S (SRE): closing loop: please reopen if you see any regression. Thanks everyone for the rapid response. :clap:
Maya (Sapphire): Will do. Really appreciate the quick help — saves our morning standup. :heart:
